behavior: Go computes the same receive address as factory.predict, checked by shared test vectors
acceptance: Foundry writes a vectors file from factory.predict for at least 20 terms (amount 1 and 2^256-1, all four testnet chain IDs, expiry 0 and 2^64-1); the Go address code matches every vector
The factory address and init-code hash are compiled into the Go binary; a contract change that alters the init code makes forge test fail until the vectors are regenerated
notes: 2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: Go address code is correct: ABI offsets for all 7 fields, OZ _cloneCodeWithImmutableArgs template (0x61 len+0x2d, prefix, impl, suffix, args), salt=keccak256(args), CREATE2 all match; 24 vectors cover amount 1/2^256-1, 4 testnet chain IDs, expiry 0/2^64-1; compiled Factory/Implementation match deployments.json v1; pnpm vectors regenerates the file byte-identical; mutating MAX_HOLD makes forge test fail with 'stale vectors'. BLOCKING: contracts check is flaky. packages/contracts/script/ReceiveAddressVectors.s.sol:21-25 calls vm.setEnv(REFUND_AUTHORITY/EXECUTOR/DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY), and test/Deploy.t.sol:13-15 sets the same process-wide env vars to different values; forge runs suites in parallel threads and Deploy.s.sol:17-18 reads env on every deployFactory() call, so the two tests race. Reproduced: first 'pnpm --filter @forwend/contracts test' failed with DeployTest.test_scriptKeepsFactoryAfterExecutorRotation 'assertion failed: 0xECe7...7546 != 0xa4Cc...AC16' (it picked up the vectors test's authority between its two deployFactory calls); 1 more failure in 10 further forge test runs. The vectors test can fail the same way with a false 'stale vectors'. Fix: stop passing config through process env in the vectors script, e.g. give Deploy a deployFactory(authority, executor) that the env-reading path and the vectors script both call. Non-blocking: Terms.IntendedChainID is uint64 while the Solidity field is uint256 (fine for real chain IDs); nothing checks the Go Factory/Implementation constants against deployments.json (only against the vectors file); Biome exclusion of vectors/ is justified because forge test compares the file byte for byte with Foundry's output.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Re-review after fix. Race fixed: script/ReceiveAddressVectors.s.sol no longer calls vm.setEnv or Deploy; it reads authority/executor from deployments.json and deploys through the CREATE2 deployer with Deploy's salt (same pattern as test/CrossChain.t.sol). Contracts check: pnpm --filter @forwend/contracts test passed (70 passed, 1 skipped), then forge test 25/25 passed (before the fix my runs failed 2 of 11). pnpm vectors regenerates the file byte-identical; factory 0xECe7...7546 and implementation 0x322F...b639 match deployments.json v1 and the Go constants. Changing MAX_HOLD in src/InvoiceTypes.sol makes forge test fail with 'stale vectors' (restored; src diff empty). Go address code still correct (ABI offsets, OZ clone template, salt=keccak256(args), CREATE2); backend check passes. 24 vectors cover acceptance line 1. No must-not-change paths touched; Deploy.s.sol, Deploy.t.sol and src unchanged. Non-blocking: SALT and CREATE2_DEPLOYER are now copied in ReceiveAddressVectors.s.sol:13-14 (also in Deploy.s.sol and CrossChain.t.sol); a salt change in Deploy alone would not show in the vectors, though the Go constants would then disagree with a new deployments.json. Terms.IntendedChainID is uint64 vs uint256 in Solidity (fine for real chain IDs). Biome exclusion of vectors/ is justified (byte-for-byte comparison).

proof.1: backend: TestReceiveMatchesFactoryPredict recomputes all 24 Foundry vectors (amount 1 and 2^256-1, chain IDs 84532/421614/5042002/42431, expiry 0 and 2^64-1) and matches each
proof.2: contracts: test_vectorsFileMatchesPredict regenerates vectors from the v1 factory and fails on any init-code change (checked by adding a function to InvoiceReceiver); backend test fails if compiled Factory/Implementation differ from the vectors file. Script uses no env vars (race with Deploy.t.sol fixed: 0/30 forge test failures, was 5/15)
